title: Classical Variation (3.Nc3)
intro: White defends e4 with 3.Nc3. Counter with 3...Nf6, break the 4.Bg5 pin with ...Be7, and strike White's centre with ...c5.

lessons.title: The Classical 3...Nf6 4.Bg5
lessons.summary: Unpin with 4...Be7, retreat ...Nfd7, and trade bishops cleanly.

steps.text: Against 3.Nc3, 3...Nf6 is a solid, classical choice that attacks e4 immediately.
Attack the e4 pawn with your king's knight.
steps.hint: Bring the g8 knight to f6.
steps.ifRight: White must deal with the attack on e4.

steps.text: White pins the knight with 4.Bg5, threatening e5.

steps.hint: Put your dark-squared bishop on e7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Be7 to unpin and prepare castling.

steps.text: Step back to d7, ready to attack White's centre with ...c5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...Nfd7: on d7 the knight supports ...c5 and ...f6.

steps.text: White trades bishops with 6.Bxe7. Recapture cleanly.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...Qxe7 so you can castle and break with ...c5.
steps.ifRight: Black castles and pushes ...c5 with a comfortable game.

lessons.title: Meeting 4.e5 (Steinitz)
lessons.summary: Step back with 4...Nfd7 and hit d4 immediately with 5...c5.

steps.text: Instead of 4.Bg5, White often closes the centre right away with 4.e5.
Retreat your knight to a useful square where it supports central breaks.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...Nfd7 so ...c5 can hit d4 right away.
steps.ifRight: In the Steinitz, Black attacks d4 with ...c5 and ...Nc6.

steps.text: White reinforces e5 and claims kingside space with 5.f4.
Attack the base of White's pawn chain immediately.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5...c5 to put pressure on d4.
steps.ifRight: Black hits d4 before White can consolidate.

steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to c6.
steps.ifRight: White's d4 pawn is under heavy pressure.

lessons.title: Meeting 4.exd5 and 7.f4
lessons.summary: Free the c8 bishop against 4.exd5 and push ...c5 after castling.

steps.text: Sometimes White relieves the central tension with 4.exd5.
Recapture to free your light-squared bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4...exd5: your c8 bishop is now completely open.

feedback.f6d5: 4...Nxd5 lets White gain central space after 5.Nxd5 exd5 6.Bd3.

steps.text: Back in the 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e5 Nfd7 6.Bxe7 Qxe7 main line, White often supports e5 with 7.f4.
Get your king to safety first, or strike at d4 right away.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...O-O (or 7...a6): ...c5 follows once White's knight cannot jump to b5.
steps.ifRight: Black is castled and ready for ...c5 and ...Nc6.

feedback.c7c5: 7...c5 at once allows 8.Nb5, aiming at c7 and d6. Castle first, then ...c5.

steps.text: After 8.Nf3, White is ready to develop Bd3 or Qd2.
Strike at White's pawn chain with your c-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8...c5 to challenge d4 and activate your pieces.
steps.ifRight: Next ...Nc6 and ...f6 undermine White's whole centre.
